overview: Liliensternus liliensterni was a large Late Triassic theropod from Germany (~210 Ma), reaching about five metres — one of the largest predatory dinosaurs of its time in Europe. Known from much of the postcranium but lacking a complete skull, it is placed among the coelophysoids or as a close relative of them, representing one of the larger members of the early theropod radiation.

The Löwenstein Formation of Germany where Liliensternus is found provides a rare glimpse into a Late Triassic European fauna otherwise poorly known. Its large size relative to contemporaries suggests that ecological niche diversification among theropods began rapidly after the origin of the group.

fossilSites.name: Löwenstein Formation
fossilSites.note: Late Triassic (Norian) fluvial and overbank deposits yielding Liliensternus material alongside early sauropodomorphs and rhynchosaurs.

articles.title: Discovery
articles.body: First described by Friedrich von Huene in 1934 as Halticosaurus liliensterni, the material was reassigned to a new genus by Welles in 1984. The specimens come from Triassic deposits in Baden-Württemberg. The partial remains are significant as among the largest Late Triassic theropods from Europe.

articles.title: Anatomy
articles.body: Known elements include cervical and dorsal vertebrae, limb bones and parts of the pelvis. The hindlimb proportions suggest a fast runner, typical of coelophysoid-grade theropods. Skull material is limited, so dietary and feeding inferences rely on comparisons with better-known relatives like Coelophysis.

articles.title: European Triassic context
articles.body: The Löwenstein Formation records a semi-arid environment with seasonal rivers — the classic Late Triassic European landscape. Liliensternus was the largest predator in a fauna that included the prosauropod Plateosaurus, various small reptiles and early mammals. Its large body size relative to Coelophysis shows that theropods quickly evolved a range of body sizes after their origin.

record.mya: late Norian, roughly 208-205 million years ago
record.description: Liliensternus liliensterni was a medium-sized early theropod from late Norian Knollenmergel beds in Thuringia, equivalent to the Trossingen Formation succession elsewhere in Germany. Its principal material comprises disarticulated partial skeletons representing at least two individuals, with only fragmentary cranial remains; a second species once assigned to it is now Lophostropheus.
facts: No complete skull or skeleton is known.
The principal L. liliensterni record is late Norian and should not be extended into the Rhaetian using former L. airelensis material.
Bipedality and carnivory are supported at broad theropod level.
Its exact position relative to coelophysoids and dilophosaur-grade theropods is unsettled.

review.ageReviewNote: Restricted to the late Norian Knollenmergel material from Thuringia; Rhaetian-Hettangian material formerly called L. airelensis belongs to Lophostropheus.
